ai.title: Refine base2 plan mode prompt to encourage multi-round clarifying
ai.summary: Updated `.agents/base2/base2.ts` plan mode instructions to explicitly permit multiple rounds of clarifying questions. The prompt now guides the agent to continue questioning until the request is fully understood, while avoiding trivial or easily changeable details. This internal change affects the `buildPlanOnlyInstructionsPrompt` function and related documentation within the base2 agent configuration.

eli5.text: The assistant that helps you plan things (like writing a story or building a project) now keeps asking follow-up questions until it really understands what you want. Instead of stopping after one round of questions, it can continue clarifying in multiple rounds, focusing only on the big important points rather than tiny details that can be easily changed later. This affects anyone using the planning mode, and you'd notice the assistant seems more thorough at making sure it gets your request right before jumping into a plan.

ai.title: Add 1s timeout to CLI exit handler
ai.summary: CLI exit handler now wraps `flushAnalytics` with a 1s timeout (`EXIT_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS`) via `withTimeout` to prevent hangs. This ensures `cleanupRenderer` and `process.exit` run promptly even if Posthog is unresponsive. Changes apply to `cli/src/hooks/use-exit-handler.ts`.

eli5.text: When you close the CLI tool, it now stops trying to send its final analytics after just one second instead of waiting indefinitely. Previously, if the analytics service was slow or unresponsive, the program could hang and delay your exit. Now you won't get stuck at the closing screen even if PostHog is being slow. This affects the command-line tool's shutdown behavior on all platforms where it runs.

ai.title: Cleanup renderer before process.exit
ai.summary: Added cleanupRenderer() calls before process.exit(0) in CLI keyboard handlers. Ensures terminal state resets correctly on Ctrl+C exit. Affects project-picker-screen.tsx and use-login-keyboard-handlers.ts.

eli5.text: When you press Ctrl+C to quit the command-line tool while picking a project, the terminal now resets to normal before closing instead of leaving garbled characters behind. You won't need to manually fix your terminal afterwards, just quit as usual and the screen will look clean. This applies only to quitting with the keyboard shortcut.

ai.title: Tab key now toggles agent mode if file menu fails
ai.summary: Tab key now triggers agent mode toggle in CLI chat when file menu open fails. Multiline input delegates tab handling to global keyboard hooks. `use-chat-keyboard.ts` adds fallback logic to `open-file-menu-with-tab` action. `keyboard-actions.ts` expands agent mode toggle condition to include `isTab` alongside `isShiftTab`.

eli5.text: When you press the Tab key while the file picker is open in the CLI chat, and that file picker fails to open, the Tab key now switches the assistant into agent mode instead of doing nothing. Previously, pressing Tab while the file menu was open would either insert a literal tab character or fail silently. The change also makes the Tab key (not just Shift+Tab) toggle agent mode when no other menus are active, so you have a more consistent way to switch modes using your keyboard. If you looked at the CLI right now, you'd notice that Tab behaves differently: it no longer gets stuck trying to open the file menu, and instead reliably flips between regular and agent modes.

ai.title: CLI input history re-reads disk before save
ai.summary: Input history now re-reads from disk before appending new entries in `use-input-history.ts`. This prevents overwriting history added by other concurrent terminal sessions. The change also ensures bash commands starting with `!` are saved to history in `router.ts`.

eli5.text: When you type a command that starts with '!' in your terminal, it now saves that command to your history so you can easily run it again later with the up and down arrows. Also, the terminal now checks your history file on disk before saving your latest command, so if you have multiple terminals open at the same time, each one will see all the commands typed in the others without overwriting each other's history.

ai.title: Fix project picker screen highlighting and sorting
ai.summary: Project picker screen updates list highlighting to use subtle theme surfaces instead of primary backgrounds, fixing contrast issues. Directory entries now sort alphabetically with Git repos highlighted via accent color. UI text simplified to 'Navigate to your project folder and press Open', and current directory path displayed in footer.

ai.title: Project picker layout adapts to short terminals
ai.summary: Refactored `project-picker-screen.tsx` to use dynamic height allocation instead of fixed thresholds, ensuring the file picker renders in short terminals. Added `COMPACT_MODE_THRESHOLD` (12 rows) to strip padding/margins and hide decorative elements (logo, help text) when space is constrained. Essential elements (input, file list, bottom bar) now receive priority over optional recents and branding. Updated input placeholder to "Select project directory...".

ai.title: Log messageHistory and systemPrompt on agent failure
ai.summary: Added messageHistory and systemPrompt to the error logging payload in packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts. This provides the full conversation context and system instructions when loopAgentSteps fails, aiding in debugging agent execution errors. Scope limited to Agent Runtime internal logging.

eli5.text: You won't notice anything different unless the assistant crashes while working. When that happens, the system now quietly records the full conversation so far plus the special instructions it was given, so whoever is fixing the problem has more context to understand what went wrong. That detailed record stays behind the scenes for troubleshooting; it does not change what you see or do in normal use.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.563 ships short terminal fixes, Tab mode toggle, disk re-read
ai.summary: This release bumps the CLI package version to 1.0.563 and bundles several user-visible improvements to the terminal interface. The project picker now adapts to short terminals via dynamic height allocation with a 12-row COMPACT_MODE_THRESHOLD, fixing rendering on constrained viewports. Tab key handling now falls through to agent mode toggling when the file menu fails to open, bash commands prefixed with ! are saved to input history, and history re-reads from disk before writes to avoid clobbering concurrent sessions. The base2 agent prompt was refined to explicitly permit multiple rounds of clarifying questions before execution.
ai.evidence: Diff shows `cli/release/package.json` version changed from "1.0.562" to "1.0.563"; release-bump commit with +1/-1 stats and no lockfile/test changes.

eli5.text: This release improves how the program picker and chat window behave in tight terminal screens, plus a few quality-of-life fixes for keyboard control and history saving. The project picker now adapts to short terminal windows by hiding logos and help text when there isn't enough room, and lists directories alphabetically with your Git projects highlighted in color. Pressing Tab while a file menu is open now toggles the agent chat mode as a backup so you are never stuck. Your typed command history is now re-read from disk before saving, which stops one terminal session from overwriting entries you added in another. The program also cleans up the terminal screen properly when you quit with Ctrl+C, and the plan-ahead assistant mode now asks follow-up questions across multiple rounds until it really understands what you want. Finally, when the autonomous agent hits an error, it logs the full conversation and instructions you gave it, which speeds up diagnosing why a task went off track.

ai.title: Preserve chat blocks on error in CLI message updater
ai.summary: Removed logic clearing `blocks` during error updates in `cli/src/utils/message-updater.ts`. Previously, errors wiped block data; now blocks are preserved for debugging context. Applies to both `createMessageUpdater` and `createBatchedMessageUpdater`.

eli5.text: When the assistant errors out while responding in the command-line version, the chat history blocks that give context to your conversation are now kept intact instead of being wiped away. This means if you look at the conversation after an error, you'll still see the structured parts of what was discussed, which helps with understanding what went wrong. The change is live today and affects anyone using the CLI when errors occur during message updates.

ai.title: Include message history in OpenRouter error log
ai.summary: Added `messages` field to the OpenRouter error logging payload in `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts`. This change captures the full message history when an upstream error occurs, aiding in debugging specific conversation states that trigger failures.

eli5.text: When the system runs into a problem while processing your chat, it now saves the full conversation history into its error log. If you ever need to dig into why a particular chat failed, you'll be able to see exactly what messages were being sent at the time. This is a behind-the-scenes improvement to help with troubleshooting.

ai.title: send-message tests expect blocks preserved
ai.summary: send-message.test.ts handleRunError assertion changed from `toBeUndefined()` to `toEqual()`. Error path now expects `aiMessage.blocks` to retain `[{ type: 'text', content: 'some block' }]` for debugging. Internal test fix only.

eli5.text: The assistant now keeps a debugging record of what was being shown when something goes wrong, instead of clearing it. This only affects the internal tests that check error handling, so if you use the assistant normally, you won't notice anything different today. However, the developers can now better trace issues because the system remembers the relevant block of content that was active during an error.
